It reminds us of the importance of self-possession and emotional steadiness, even in the face of adversity or chaos. This is particularly relevant to the many Muslims living in challenging social, political, or economic circumstances.

historical_references.reference: Mahul was an important seaport city in the Islamic world during the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 CE). It was located in present-day Bahrain and was known for its strategic position at the crossroads of maritime trade between the Indian Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea. Mahul was a major hub for the trade of pearls, textiles, spices, and other commodities.

During the Fatimid Caliphate (909-1171 CE), Mahul was a significant naval base and military stronghold. The Fatimids used Mahul as a base to launch naval expeditions against their enemies, particularly the Byzantines and the Crusaders. Mahul's strategic location in the Persian Gulf made it an essential defensive position for the Fatimids against seaborne threats.
